text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government-linked Neptune Orient Lines is buying U.S. shipping group APL Ltd at Singapore $1.2 billion, the largest foreign acquisition by a Singapore firm.
- Tiger Woods crowned United States Masters champion, youngest winner in history, finishing with a 69 and winning by 12 shots at the Augusta National Golf Club.
- Three-year-old toddler dies when run over by a lorry as he dashes across road.
- Taiwanese-owned Sinoca Electronics Group goes into receivership and has appointed KPMG Peat Marwick as receiver.
- Competition in car loans market has moved to high gear with Bank of America's introduction of new scheme allowing borrowers to start off with low monthly payment.
- Singapore stocks fall drastically on Monday in line with Wall Street tumble.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore waives requirement for shareholder approval of Neptune Orient Lines APL takeover.
- Property shares lose further ground despite government's latest property curbs being less severe than expected.
- Stock markets in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur plunge following wave of bearish sentiment on lending curbs.
- Singapore International Airlines confirms discussion with Air New Zealand on a "commercial relationship" but declines to elaborate.
- MMI Holdings initial public offer subscribed 4.22 times. - Sembawang Corp says its takeover bid for Jurong Shipyard may include an alternative of both shares and cash.

- Sesdaq-listed electronics contract manufacturer Venture Manufacturing and Electronic Resources get approval from Stock Exchange of Singapore for main board listing, and more companies may follow suit.
- Keppel Fels announces Singapore $328 million floating production, storage and offloading vessel, scheduled for delivery in early 1998, is near completion.
